title: The Inverted Canopy Descent

features.name: the-roots-that-climb
features.desc-on-touch: Roots ascending into sky-softness, still drawing nourishment from the air-soil that presses down from above. You cannot tell if they are reaching or recoiling. The inversion is complete and has forgotten itself.

features.name: the-canopy-now-underfoot
features.desc-on-touch: The leaf-mass you stand upon was always the sky here. When you press your heel, it springs back with soft resistance of growth. The canopy beneath you is still breathing its photosynthesis upward into the darkness below.

features.name: the-masks-hung-in-the-air
features.desc-on-touch: Cloth faces suspended where they fell or rose—impossible to say which. Each one teaches you something about refusal, about watching without being watched. The masks move on currents you cannot see.

features.name: the-light-that-falls-upward
features.desc-on-touch: Luminescence rising from the darkness above, casting shadows on the underside of your thoughts. The trees remember light from before gravity had a preference.

features.name: the-song-that-reverses-itself-on-descent
features.desc-on-touch: A melody plays in the order you forgot it. Each note is the echo of the note that will follow it. The grove is teaching you to hear backwards.

inscription: the grove has learned that falling teaches you the grammar of gravity, and then teaches you to unlearn it

file.name: Canopy_Inversion_Sequence_Notes.txt
file.note: Field observations from within the inverted grove. Each note is indexed to its own opposite. The observer becomes the observed. The notebook contains only this sentence, repeated with deepening sincer

exits.label: back toward the groves learning to walk away
higher into the roots that have learned the sky's alphabet
toward the layer where down and up are forgetting their difference
